Get a summary of a GTFS feed

Source: R/get_summary.R
get_summary.Rd

Runs a set of diagnostics on a GTFS feed (optionally restricted to some dates, routes, modes, agencies and a time of day), writes them to a report with tables and figures, renders the report to HTML and opens it in the browser (in interactive sessions). The diagnostics are also returned as a list of data.tables. This function does not validate or look for quality issues in the GTFS feed. To do that, use validate_gtfs().

Usage

get_summary(
  gtfs,
  date = NULL,
  route_id = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  agency = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  output_dir = NULL,
  open_browser = TRUE,
  by_route_type = FALSE
)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs(), or the path to a GTFS file.

date

A Date vector (including IDate) or a character vector of dates in the "YYYYMMDD" or "YYYY-MM-DD" formats. If given, only the services that run on these dates are described. If NULL (the default), the whole period covered by the feed is described.

route_id

A character vector. If given, only these routes are described. If NULL (the default), all routes are described.

mode

An integer vector of route_types (see filter_by_route_type()) or a character vector of mode names ("tram", "subway", "rail", "bus", "ferry", "cable_tram", "aerial_lift", "funicular", "trolleybus" and "monorail", which correspond to the basic route_types). If given, only routes of these modes are described. If NULL (the default), all modes are described.

agency

A character vector of agency_ids. If given, only the services of these agencies are described. If NULL (the default), all agencies are described.

from, to

Strings in the "HH:MM:SS" format. If given (both must be), only the trips that run within this time of day are described. If NULL (the default), the whole day is described.

output_dir

A string. The directory in which the report is saved (created if needed). If NULL (the default), a gtfstools directory inside tempdir() is used. Existing reports in this directory are overwritten.

open_browser

A logical. Whether to open the HTML report in the browser, in interactive sessions (defaults to TRUE).

by_route_type

A logical. Whether to break down the totals, speeds, distances and frequencies by transport mode (route_type), in addition to the whole selection (defaults to FALSE).

Value

A named list of data.tables (invisibly, if the report was opened in the browser):

  • files: the tables in the feed (file) and their number of rows (n_rows), before any filtering;

  • agency: the agency_id, agency_name, agency_timezone, agency_url and agency_lang columns (those present in the feed) of the agencies that run the selected trips (all agencies, if the selected routes have no agency_id);

  • services: a single row summarising the calendar of the selected services, with the columns start_date and end_date (the first and last days with service), n_days (the number of days between them, both included), n_service_days (the number of days with service), n_services (the number of service_ids), mean_trips_per_day (over the days with service), busiest_date and max_trips_per_day (the day with the most trips and its number of trips) and feed_start_date and feed_end_date (from feed_info, NA if absent);

  • totals: the columns indicator, value and unit, with the number of agencies, routes, trips and stops, the total and mean length of the shapes and of the trips (in km), the total duration of the trips (in hours), the mean duration of the trips (in minutes), the mean trip speed (in km/h) and the mean route headway (in minutes). The means are taken over the shapes and trips whose value is known. If by_route_type = TRUE, value is replaced by one column per mode followed by the column all (codes of extended route_types, such as "700", are non-syntactic names, so they need backticks);

  • speed, distance and frequency: summary statistics (n, min, q25, median, mean, q75, max and unit) of the trip speeds (in km/h), of the trip lengths (in km) and of the route headways (in minutes). frequency also has the columns date, from and to, with the day and the time of day in which the headways were measured. If by_route_type = TRUE, these tables start with a mode column and have one row per mode followed by the row all.

The report is saved as gtfs_summary.md and gtfs_summary.html (together with its figures) in output_dir.

Details

The report requires the {ggplot2}, {knitr} and {rmarkdown} packages, and Pandoc, which is shipped with RStudio.

The feed is filtered by agency, mode, route, date and time of day, in this order. The time-of-day filter keeps the whole trips that run within it (see filter_by_time_of_day() with full_trips = TRUE), so the trip speeds and lengths refer to whole trips.

Trip lengths, durations and speeds are calculated with get_trip_length(), get_trip_duration() and get_trip_speed(). Each trip is counted once, however many days it runs on and however many departures the frequencies table lists for it. Trips with a zero or negative duration count in the total and mean durations, but have no speed. The total and mean shape lengths count each shape used by the selected trips once, and the number of stops counts the stops visited by the selected trips.

The services summary and the calendar chart in the report describe the whole calendar of the selected services: when date is given, the services that run on these dates are kept as a whole (see filter_by_date()), so they may also cover other days. The number of trips on each day is calculated as in get_calendar_overlap(), counting each departure listed in frequencies.

Route headways are calculated with get_route_frequency(), by route (and by direction_id, if the field is present in the trips table), on a single day: the day with the most trips among the given dates, or in the whole feed if date is NULL (the earliest one, in case of ties). They are measured within the given time of day or, if from and to are NULL, from the first to the last departure of that day, rounded out to whole hours. Trips that start on the previous day and run after midnight are not counted, and times are in the local time of each agency.

With by_route_type = TRUE, modes are named as in the mode argument, extended route_types by their code, and trips whose route_type is unknown are grouped as "unknown". Modes are ordered by route_type, with "unknown" last. Each mode is described as if it were selected alone (except that the headways of all modes are measured on the same day and time of day), so stops, shapes and agencies shared by several modes count in each of them. Only the numbers of routes and trips and the total trip lengths and durations add up to the all column. Modes whose routes have blank agency_ids count all the agencies of the selection, and trips listed in stop_times but not in trips only count in all. In the report, the histograms of the modes are overlaid.

Examples

if (
  requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) &&
    rmarkdown::pandoc_available()
) {
  data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")

  feed_summary <- get_summary(
    data_path,
    output_dir = tempdir(),
    open_browser = FALSE
  )
  feed_summary$totals

  # \donttest{
  feed_summary <- get_summary(
    data_path,
    mode = "bus",
    from = "07:00:00",
    to = "09:00:00",
    output_dir = tempdir(),
    open_browser = FALSE
  )
  feed_summary$frequency

  feed_summary <- get_summary(
    data_path,
    output_dir = tempdir(),
    open_browser = FALSE,
    by_route_type = TRUE
  )
  feed_summary$totals
  # }
}
